n.quote: Replication results: In the replication experiment, 35.0% (se = 1.4%; n = 1192) of the participants in the gift/no-image condition chose to donate, whereas only 30.1% (se = 1.3%; n = 1249) donated in the gift/image condition. As in the original study, the difference between conditions (4.8 percentage points, se = 1.9) was tested using an independent-samples t-test assuming equal variances: (t(2439) = 2.575, p = 0.010; n = 2441). As a result, we can reject the null hypothesis of no difference in donation rates between the condition in which the gift card is visible and the condition in which the gift card is not visible. The standardized effect size (Cohen’s d) is d = 0.104 (95% CI [0.025, 0.184]).

reported_success.quote: Discussion: Given the criteria and procedure outlined above, the hypothesis of interest has been successfully replicated at a significance level of p < 0.05.
